question: What's the right pricing strategy for a freemium → paid conversion?
answer:
**Direct Answer:** Freemium converts at 3–7% to paid; set premium tier 8–12x higher than free feature value. Conversion rate depends on free-to-paid gap clarity, feature lockouts, and seat-count friction. Tier pricing at $10/user, $35/user, $99/user for SMB freemium-sourced traffic. **The Detail** Freemium is a **customer acquisition funnel**, not a pricing strategy. Most founders price incorrectly by not locking enough value behind the paywall. **Freemium-to-paid conversion formula:** **Conversion Rate = (% who hit free tier limit) × (% who value next tier) × (% who accept price)** Example breakdown: - Free users who hit 100-doc limit: 40% - Those who need more docs: 60% of that cohort = 24% - Those who accept $99/mo pricing: 50% of that = 12% freemium conversion **Common mistakes:** 1. **Too much value in free tier** — If free tier supports 90% of use cases, conversion tanks. Ideal: free handles one persona/use case fully; other personas blocked. (Notion does this: free personal note-taker, paid for team collab.) 2. **Unclear price-to-value anchor** — Freemium users don't price-shop like trial users; they compare features not dollars. Set the first paid tier just above where most free users exceed limits (usually 2–3x usage or higher seat count). 3. **Seat expansion friction** — If free = 1 user and paid starts at $35/user/mo for teams, require $280/mo for a 5-person team. That's friction. Tier it: $35 (1 user), $99 (3 users), $199 (5+ users unlimited). **Freemium pricing by segment:** | Use Case | Free Limit | Entry Paid | Mid Tier | Enterprise | |----------|------------|-----------|----------|------------| | Note-taking (1 user) | Unlimited | $9/mo (family) | $15/mo (team) | Custom | | Analytics (5 seats) | 1 seat, 7 days | $29/mo (3 seats) | $99/mo (10 seats) | Custom | | API (SMB dev) | 10k req/mo | $49/mo (1M req/mo) | $299/mo (10M) | Custom | **Drivers of conversion lift:** 1. **Feature scarcity vs quantity** — Tier by features (advanced export, SSO, API), not just volume. Tier by power-user tools: advanced reporting, custom fields, integrations. 2. **Usage-based insert** — If $35/mo (fixed) feels too high for monthly-active users <20, charge $1/user/mo capped at $35. Removes sticker shock. 3. **Freemium data for pricing power** — Track: feature adoption by segment, free-to-paid conversion by feature, cohort LTV. Adjust pricing quarterly. **Action steps:** - Run cohort analysis: % of free users hitting each feature limit (docs, seats, API calls) - Price paid tiers 2–3x above where 60% of free users plateau - Test in-app paywalls 30 days before tier limit ("Upgrade in 30 days to keep access") - Monitor: conversion rate, ARPU, LTV.
